entries.label: v0.1.21
entries.title: A home for your garden, wherever you play

sections.heading: Garden fixes
items: Both players begin with no tool equipped.
Turned the arrival rabbit to face its direction of travel.

sections.heading: Accounts and cloud-save integration
items: Added an Account & Cloud screen with email registration, sign-in, password-reset requests and sign-out.
Added explicit local/cloud garden selection, automatic syncing after local saves, revision-conflict protection and local backups before cloud downloads. Offline play remains available.
Added a private Your Valley website dashboard showing uploaded coins, animal population, XP, land coverage and wildlife visit/residency dates.

Supabase database setup is installed and signed-out access is denied. Redirect URLs are configured; public account launch still needs email delivery, live authenticated acceptance checks and manual publication.

blog.intro: The rabbit has stopped attempting a moonwalk, and your spirit now arrives without immediately brandishing a hoe. Meanwhile, the valley is getting cloud saves. These clouds have considerably better filing cabinets than the ones Arthur complains about.
why: Starting with empty hands gives the first arrival room to breathe. The rabbit correction makes its little crossing read as an actual journey rather than a disagreement with physics.

The new account screen and private Valley Club dashboard let one garden follow its owner across devices. Coins, wildlife and progress belong together; nobody should need a spreadsheet to remember which hedgehog moved in.
Choosing a local or cloud garden is deliberate, and older uploads cannot silently overwrite newer ones. A backup stays on the computer before a cloud download replaces its local save.
issues: The development integration is ready for account testing, but the website and game have not been published. Redirect URLs are configured; a working confirmation and recovery email sender is still required before public registration.
Live checks confirmed that signed-out access is denied. Game save/restore and mocked account/dashboard tests passed; two-account authenticated database and real email delivery tests remain pending.
Sign-in is session-only for now. The dashboard shows the last uploaded snapshot, and cloud conflicts pause syncing until the player chooses how to resolve them.

Local website preview: the private Valley Club sign-in page, before any garden is uploaded.

entries.label: v0.1.20
entries.title: Familiar faces at the garden gate

sections.heading: Arrival scenery
items: Replaced the crossing placeholder with the supplied rabbit, the flying placeholder with the animated robin, and the distant animals with the supplied bull model.
Added a textured rock outside each garden corner, with varied rotations that stay consistent when reloading.
Arthur now waits beside the northern entrance for your first arrival and returns to wandering after his welcome.
Reduced the rock’s game mesh detail while preserving its original source model and texture.

sections.heading: Studio notes
items: Updated the latest blog post with the previous Blender robin animation work and a dated development follow-up covering these arrival improvements.

blog.intro: The temporary rabbit has handed in its notice. A proper rabbit has taken the role, the robin has brought its newly animated wings, and the bulls have agreed to stand in the distance looking as though they own the place. Arthur, meanwhile, has finally checked the arrival time.
why: The first arrival established the route and camera timing. Replacing its stand-ins with the supplied models makes those little look-around moments belong to the valley. The flying robin reuses the Blender animation made from the two motion references.

Four rocks give the garden corners a little visual definition without bringing back the perimeter wall. Their varied angles are repeatable, so loading a saved garden does not cause a geological reshuffle.
Arthur now waits beside the northern entrance until his welcome finishes. Being greeted is rather more welcoming when the greeter has not wandered off halfway through your approach.
issues: The rabbit and bull sources contain rigs but no animation clips. The rabbit currently uses a simple whole-body hop; the bulls have subtle breathing movement. Their full skeletal gait animations are still future work.
These arrival animals are scenery, not purchased livestock or new visitor discoveries. The robin’s separate wildlife visit still needs 1% water.
A missing texture connection on the rock was corrected during import. The original source models and textures remain intact.

sections.heading: A walk into the valley
items: Added a gravel pathway following the northern mountains and hills down to the garden edge, using the supplied gravel textures.
New gardens now begin with a short downhill camera walk, gentle footstep bobbing and smooth looks toward a crossing creature, passing bird, birch tree and two distant animals.
The arrival leads into Arthur’s welcome. Escape, B / Circle or Start skips the walk; existing gardens receive the path without replaying the arrival.
Time, weather and ambience continue throughout the shared arrival, with normal single-player or split-screen play restored afterwards. The scenery placeholders do not count as wildlife visits.

blog.intro: Previously, arriving in the garden involved the traditional Welsh practice of appearing out of thin air. We have now installed a path. The rabbit-shaped object using it has declined to pay council tax.
why: A new garden should feel like somewhere you have travelled to. The gravel approach connects the northern mountain scenery to the plot, while a short walk gives the valley a chance to introduce itself before Arthur does.

The camera follows the actual hillside surface, with a small walking bob and eased turns. Four staged moments give the journey a little life: something crosses your path, a bird passes, a birch catches your eye, and two animals stand further away.

Early captures showed grass growing through the new gravel. Admirable botanical enthusiasm, but rather poor path maintenance. We cleared the route and moved nearby tree placements back so the approach reads more clearly.
issues: The creatures and bird are deliberately simple placeholders. Their motion is staged for the arrival; they are not new collectible animals, residents or Field Guide discoveries. The birch uses the existing tree model.
The walk follows the lower approach. The upper mountain path is background scenery, and normal player movement remains inside the garden boundary.
Automated checks cover completion, skipping, existing-garden loading, continued clock updates and split-screen restoration. Physical controller testing is still needed.

sections.heading: Menus and button hints
items: Restored the clean woodland-green garden pause and village shop menus, removing the decorative petal borders.
Button hints now float beside the analogue clock, with outlined text for contrast against the scenery. The daffodil tool wheel and its controller controls stay in place.

sections.heading: Notes from the studio
items: Added a website blog by Waldas Gamer Studios, with release stories, reasons for changes, recorded issues and development screenshots.
Manual publishing now creates one blog post per new release and includes it in the website update.

blog.intro: The menus had dressed for a flower show. Lovely ambition; rather a lot of elbows at the tea table. We have asked the decorative borders to take the afternoon off and given the valley a little breathing room.
why: The decorative frames made the pause and shop menus feel busier than intended. Following player feedback, those panels return to their simpler woodland-green appearance. The daffodil tool wheel keeps its petals because they are the actual selections, rather than extra decoration.
Button hints now sit directly over the scene. A dark text outline helps them stay readable against bright skies and pale ground, without putting another box between you and the garden.

The changelog tells you what changed. This blog adds the why, the rough edges, and screenshots where we have them. Each manual release now preserves its own studio note, so the story will not quietly turn into next week’s story.
issues: Controller icons follow the device name reported by the driver. A PlayStation controller presented as a virtual Xbox pad will still show Xbox symbols. Hardware-specific behaviour needs checking on real controllers; the automated checks simulate input.
The new menu treatment follows feedback on the last update. Sometimes the most productive gardening tool is an eraser. No saved-garden format changes are needed for this update.

screenshots.caption: Development build: the garden pause menu returns to its clean woodland-green style.
Development build: the daffodil tool wheel stays, with button hints floating beside the analogue clock.

sections.heading: Daffodil interface and tools
items: Open and confirm the new tool wheel with Xbox A / PlayStation Cross; close it with B / Circle. Tab opens it on keyboard. Shovel selection leads to its four modes.
Faceted daffodil petals surround a parchment tool hub. The selected petal grows and glows; a softly blurred twilight-green backdrop stays within the player’s half of split-screen.

An analogue clock on the left shows the shared garden level. Twelve petals fill towards each new level, with 100 XP per level. Gardening, animal visits, residency and births earn saved XP; repeated tile actions are capped each day.

Contextual prompts beside the clock use the supplied Xbox or PlayStation artwork based on each controller’s reported identity. Pause and shop menus use matching parchment, serif text and gold petal frames. Existing saves start with zero XP and remain compatible.

entries.label: v0.1.15
entries.title: A warm welcome to the valley

sections.heading: Arthur and the valley
items: Arthur welcomes you whenever you enter or return to the garden, playing Welcome.mp3 with a face-on camera, alternating talking animations and timed subtitles. The camera returns to normal afterwards.
Speech bubbles have a daffodil border using alternating Border-1 and Border-2 artwork with staggered angles. Welcome and hedgehog conversations queue separately.
The main menu now uses the same rolling ridges, mountain geometry, grass and stone material system as the garden, with its moving birds and changing sky.

sections.heading: Interface and weather
items: Removed keyboard and controller reminders from the HUD, pause menus, Field Guide and speech pause display. Tool names, compass headings, time and weather remain visible.
Unified panel and button styling, tidied pause and options layouts, added a dimmed pause backdrop and scrollable shop lists, and matched the split-screen status panels.

Natural weather now chooses from weighted transitions with variable durations. Clear spells can linger and showers can ease, return or build into storms; the garden and village continue to share one weather state.
Weather timing and random state persist in saves. Existing saves remain supported.

sections.heading: Launcher
items: The launcher displays scrollable patch notes for the latest published version and keeps a saved copy available offline.
Future manual releases use the website changelog as their player-facing GitHub release notes. Failed note retrieval does not block updates or playing the installed game.

sections.heading: Local co-op
items: Connect two controllers for automatic side-by-side play in the garden and village. Each spirit has its own movement, camera, tool selection and shovel mode.
Player one keeps the gold-and-blue spirit; player two uses the original red-and-gold spirit. Both can tend the same garden with continuous tool use.
Pause menus, the Field Guide, shop interiors and story conversations are shared. Disconnecting a controller returns to one view and pauses safely; reconnecting restores the second spirit.
Existing gardens remain compatible. Player two’s garden position, selected tool and shovel mode are saved with the shared garden.

sections.heading: Wildlife
items: Added the supplied robin model and plumage texture, with gentle hopping and pecking movements.
Robins wait outside and visit when water and deep-water tiles cover at least 1% of the garden (13 tiles in the current plot). Temporary rain puddles do not count.
The first actual entry triggers a visitor notice and unlocks the robin’s 3D Field Guide preview and visit day. Visits and position persist across saved games.

entries.label: v0.1.12
entries.title: Direct tools, gentler ground and subtitle fixes

sections.heading: Changed
items: Select Hoe, Seeds, Watering Can and Shovel with 1–4, or D-pad Up, Right, Down and Left. The radial tool menu is retired.
Cycle shovel modes with X on keyboard or X / Square on controller. Put tools away with T or B / Circle; B still goes back in menus.
Natural garden rises are capped at 18 cm. Older saved raised patches are softened once; dug-out areas retain their depth.
Thump sets every corner and edge of the selected micro-tile to height zero, with a transition into neighbouring ground.

sections.heading: Fixed
items: Arthur’s speech bubble stays hidden until he speaks, including after entering the garden or returning from the village.
Putting a tool away cancels its current stroke, particles and sound. Ctrl+T still controls the TARDIS.

sections.heading: Website
items: Added this development changelog and linked it from the game page. Future completed changes will receive notes before manual publication.

sections.heading: Added
items: The first hedgehog visit starts a face-on conversation with Arthur.
Arthur alternates his two supplied talking animations while Arthur_Hedgehogs.mp3 plays. A speech bubble displays subtitles generated from the recording.
The camera and controls return when the recording ends. The scene waits for menus, supports pausing, and saves completion so it only plays once per garden.

sections.heading: Added
items: Village mountains, wooded ridges, meadow verges, grass, drifting clouds and mist, using the garden’s landscape assets.
The village and shops share the garden’s clock and weather, including night lighting, rain, wet surfaces, thunder and ambient sound.

sections.heading: Improved
items: Gravel street edges blend into the meadow.
Gold-and-blue spirit cursors replace the red-and-gold colours. Their mesh follows the ground as they move, rotate and resize.
Fixed village cursor visibility and shop selection; the ring frames the selected shop.

sections.heading: Improved
items: Garden-edge textures continue into the surrounding meadow and blend over 1.5 metres, including corners. Changes to edge tiles appear immediately outside the boundary.
Colour, normal detail, roughness, parallax and wetness match at the join.
Thump flattens the whole micro-tile, including its corners and shared edges. The next update changes its target height to zero.

sections.heading: Added
items: The shovel has four animated modes with sound: Dig, Pick, Pour and Thump.
Dig deforms the ground into a sloping, water-filled hollow. Pick makes a small seed hole; Pour restores dirt; Thump levels the ground.
Hold left-click or right trigger to keep using tools while gliding. Each tool uses its supplied sound effects.
Ctrl+T and right-stick click toggle the TARDIS landing and takeoff.

sections.heading: Improved
items: Data collision, water depth and grass roots follow edits. Deformation and seed holes survive saving and loading.
Release packaging now exports to a fresh staging file and excludes temporary packs.

entries.label: v0.1.7
entries.title: Garden milestones and a land survey

sections.heading: Added
items: Bottom-left notices report animal visits, residency and recorded birth or death events. Visit and residency dates appear in the Field Guide.
A Land Area category maps all 1,296 micro-tiles, with ground-type counts and percentages.

sections.heading: Changed
items: The TARDIS lands just north of the garden, facing south, without spinning.

sections.heading: Development note
items: Birth and death notifications are event support; automatic breeding and ageing are not implemented.

sections.heading: Added
items: Compasses in the garden and village show the direction you face.
A developer console opens with the backtick key and accepts time and weather commands.
The supplied TARDIS model has materialisation, lighting and landing/takeoff sound effects, with console controls.

sections.heading: Changed
items: New gardens begin without animals inside. A wild hedgehog patrols outside until grass covers at least 1% of the plot.
The hedgehog becomes a resident at 5% grass coverage. The Field Guide records first visit and residency days, saved with the garden.

sections.heading: Added
items: The peacock joins the animal shop, using the supplied model and animated movement.

sections.heading: Changed
items: Garden movement becomes continuous, like the village, instead of snapping the player to micro-tiles. Tools still work on the underlying tile grid.
New gardens begin as hard dirt.

sections.heading: Added
items: Grass and stone textures, plus grass tufts, extend onto the surrounding scenery and menu landscape.

sections.heading: Improved
items: Removed the cottage from the garden and expanded the textured surrounding scenery.
The 3D menu has a fuller natural environment; imported models respond to lighting and weather through shared material effects.
Added a way to put the current tool away.

sections.heading: Improved
items: Natural rolling terrain replaces the uniformly flat garden surface. Ground materials are less shiny.
Improved the cloud and star sky, distant wisps and water rendering.
Grass follows the ground’s surface height.

sections.heading: Added
items: The supplied logo becomes the game and launcher icon.
A refreshed launcher shows the installed game version and download progress.
A public game page provides the Windows launcher download.
Batched 3D grass adds depth to grassy ground.

sections.heading: Garden and tools
items: Started with exportable 2 m ground chunks, each divided into nine micro-tiles, and expanded the garden to 24 × 24 metres.
Connected dirt, hard dirt, grass, long grass, water, deep water, path and stone materials; height-map parallax adds surface detail.
A low-floating spirit replaces the visible player, with mouse camera aiming, object selection and a resizing swirling cursor.
Added Hoe, Seed Packet and Watering Can models with animated use, seed and water particles, gardening interactions and saved progress.

sections.heading: People and wildlife
items: Imported Arthur and Meera with animation cycles, plus Angus and a valley visitor. Turning is smooth and NPCs avoid one another.
Added chicken, hedgehog, badger and dragon models, including procedural movement for rigged animals.
Weather-responsive shivering and talking animation/audio behaviour were explored with the visitor models.

sections.heading: Sky and sound
items: Twenty-minute days and twenty-minute nights, a moving sun, clock, stars and a changing sky.
Fair, cloudy, light rain, rain, heavy rain, thunderstorm and clearing weather, with wet ground and rain puddles.
Birds, wind, stream and storm ambience replaced the music. Layered Welsh mountains, woodland, mist, heather, ferns and gorse frame the garden.
Prototype music, the perimeter wall and fixed pond were retired as the open garden took shape.

sections.heading: Menus, guide and village
items: A 16:9 presentation and animated 3D mountain main menu, with birds, day/night weather, the golden CWTCH title and “your slice of the valley.” tagline.
Main-menu entry, new garden, options and quit controls; pause-menu Save & Quit.
An old leather Field Guide opens from its cover with animated pages, handwritten styling, 3D previews and descriptions for people, animals and plants.
Controller movement, camera, menu navigation, shoulder-button categories and directional entry selection.
A gravel village street leads to animal, plant, decoration and building shops, with cottage exteriors, interiors, purchases and delivery to the garden.

sections.heading: Development and installation
items: The desktop CWTCH folder became the canonical development project, with source assets, full source documentation and reproducible builds.
Windows launcher installation and updates use versioned packages and download checksums; saves are kept separately.
